entries.definition: showing intellectual penetration or emotional depth
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The strongest of these and the widest, crediting either a mind that cuts through or a feeling that runs deep, where *deep* and *thoughtful* stay with the intellect.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Mild, steady approval for possessing intellectual depth, without the reach *profound* claims.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm approval - what accords with custom is credited with grace rather than mere compliance, unlike the dry *decorous*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Gentle and pleased - it finds conduct agreeable in its accord with propriety rather than measuring it against a rule.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A phrase rather than a word, and formal to the point of ceremony - approval delivered by invoking the code instead of describing the conduct.
examples: it is not comme il faut for a gentleman to be constantly asking for money

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval as a verdict - the social rule was met, and nothing warmer than that is claimed.

entries.definition: in harmony with the spirit of particular persons or occasion
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Modest and human - it grants that a thing suits the persons and the moment, with less deliberation than *fitting*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cool and external - conduct is held up against a standard of propriety and passes, with none of the warmth of *becoming*.

entries.definition: in harmony with the spirit of particular persons or occasion
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval keyed to the occasion and the people in it rather than to any code - it praises harmony where *correct* praises compliance.
examples: we have come to dedicate a portion of that field … It is altogether fitting and proper that we should do this

entries.definition: proper or legitimate according to Muslim law
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A designation rather than a compliment - it states that something is proper or legitimate under a named law, and the approval belongs to that law and not to the speaker.
examples: the fund earns halal profits in full compliance with the Shari'a

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and reassuring - declares a thing proper or legitimate, above board and open to no objection.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous - the excess of propriety is read as self-satisfaction, correctness worn as superiority over others.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest fault in this group - propriety held so tightly it stiffens, mocked rather than condemned.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Dismissive and faintly ridiculing - the overdone propriety is treated as fussiness, silly rather than severe like *priggish*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Propriety inflated into squeamishness - more disapproving than *prim*, since the excess is taken as a readiness to be shocked.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The bluntest way to render the same social judgement as *correct*, carrying no formality at all.
examples: it isn't right to leave the party without saying goodbye

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Understated - grants that conduct accords with propriety without the ceremony *decorous* brings to the same verdict.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: States only that the purpose is fixed and passes no verdict on it, where *steadfast* and *stalwart* praise.
examples: bent on going to the theater

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Determination pushed to its extreme edge, where the resolve looks driven rather than chosen.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Says the will outright and says there is a lot of it, with none of the hardness metaphor carried by *firm* or *stiff*.
examples: a struggle against a determined enemy

entries.definition: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Resolution felt as something pressed against and not giving - resistance where *steady* offers only constancy.

entries.definition: firm in purpose or belief; characterized by firmness and determination
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and settled, and it covers belief as well as purpose - firmness treated as a standing quality of the person, not a stand taken once.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Dependability raised to staunchness - stronger praise than *stout*, and it suggests standing by as well as standing up.
examples: a stalwart supporter of the UN

entries.definition: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The warmest of the unshakable four - firmness praised as something held faithfully over time.

entries.definition: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The evenest word here - determination as a level that never dips, without the hardness *firm* and *stiff* put into it.
examples: Steady to his purpose, he scarcely spoke ten words to her through the whole of Saturday

entries.definition: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Unshakable, but by rigidity - the resolve reads as unbending as much as strong.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Hearty approval - dependable in the way something sturdy is, solid enough to take weight.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The purpose holds against something that might have cowed it - it implies the attempt was made and failed.
